'''Cherfilus-McCormick:''' {{legend0|#584cde|70–80%}} {{legend0|#3933e5|80–90%}} | title = U.S. Representative{{-}} | before_election = [[Alcee Hastings]] | before_party = [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] | after_election = [[Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick]] | after_party = [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] }} {{Elections in Florida sidebar}} The '''2022 Florida's 20th congressional district special election''' was a special election to the [[United States House of Representatives]]. The seat had been vacant since incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] representative [[Alcee Hastings]] died on April 6, 2021, of [[pancreatic cancer]].{{cite web|last=Nicol|first=Ryan|date=April 6, 2021|title=Alcee Hastings dies at 84 after cancer battle|url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/395348-hastings-dies-84-cancer-battle|access-date=April 6, 2021|website=Florida Politics}} The special election was scheduled by [[Governor of florida|Governor]] [[Ron DeSantis]] to be held on January 11, 2022. The primary elections were held on November 2, 2021. This left the seat vacant for nine months, substantially longer than the delay for previous special elections.{{cite web | url=https://www.tampabay.com/news/florida-politics/2021/05/04/desantis-sets-election-for-hastings-seat-in-2022-leaving-it-open-for-9-months/ | title=DeSantis sets election for Hastings' seat in 2022, leaving it open for 9 months }} Following a recount, Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick was declared the winner of the Democratic primary by five votes over [[Broward County]] [[County Commissioner|Commissioner]] [[Dale Holness]]. Cherfilus-McCormick easily defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Jason Mariner]] in the January 11, 2022 special election, winning 79% of the popular vote. ==Democratic primary== Shevrin Jones with 3%}} |{{party shading/Undecided}}|'''50%''' |- |– |– |– |11% |7% |– |{{party shading/Democratic}}|'''14%''' |14%{{efn|Bobby Powell with 10%; Shevrin Jones with 4%}} |{{party shading/Undecided}}|'''53%''' |- |– |– |– |'''15%''' |11% |– |'''15%''' |– |{{party shading/Undecided}}|'''59%''' |} ===Results=== Per Florida law, because the margin separating Cherfilus-McCormick and Holness was less than 0.5%, a [[recount]] was held.{{cite news |title=Democratic primary to replace Alcee Hastings is too close to call |first=Alex |last=Daugherty |work=Miami Herald |date=November 3, 2021 |access-date=November 4, 2021 |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/news/politics-government/article255310276.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20211103054732/https://www.miamiherald.com/news/politics-government/article255310276.html |archive-date=November 3, 2021}} Ballots received by November 12 from overseas were accepted. The two candidates were two votes apart as some ballots that had been cast were still in dispute.{{cite web|url=https://www.wlrn.org/news/2021-11-05/florida-us-congressional-district-dale-holness-sheila-cherfilus-mccormick-alcee-hastings-broward-palm-beach|title=Vote lead continues to change in Florida U.S. congressional primary recount|website=[[WLRN-FM]]|first1=Daniel|last1=Rivero|date=November 5, 2021|accessdate=November 12, 2021}} On November 12, over a week after the primary, the [[Broward County, Florida|Broward County]] canvassing board declared Cherfilus-McCormick the winner after a recount failed to change the vote totals. However, Holness did not immediately [[concession (politics)|concede]], pointing out that the board had rejected twelve [[Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act|overseas military ballots]]. He said he would confer with a lawyer to decide whether or not to challenge the results.{{cite news|last=Murray|first=Joan|title=Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick Wins Democratic Primary Race For District 20|url=https://miami.cbslocal.com/2021/11/12/sheila-cherfilus-mccormick-emergency-motion-district-20-seat/|work=[[WFOR-TV]]|date=November 12, 2021}} The [[Palm Beach County, Florida|Palm Beach County]] canvassing board voted to certify the election results on the same day.{{cite news|last1=Burke|first1=Peter|last2=Sczesny|first2=Matt|title=Palm Beach County Canvassing Board certifies results for special primary election|url=https://www.wptv.com/news/political/elections-local/judge-rejects-sheila-cherfilus-mccormick-request-to-stop-counting-3-vote-by-mail-ballots-in-democratic-congressional-race|work=[[WPTV-TV]]|date=November 12, 2021}} State officials certified the results on November 16. Cherfilus-McCormick prevailed by five votes.{{cite web|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/581752-florida-officials-certify-winner-in-primary-for-alcee-hastings-seat-after-5|title=Florida officials certify 5-vote victory in primary for Alcee Hastings' seat|website=The Hill|last1=Greenwood|first1=Max|date=November 16, 2021}} Cherfilus-McCormick won in [[Palm Beach County, Florida|Palm Beach County]], receiving 30% of the vote. Meanwhile, Holness won in [[Broward County, Florida|Broward County]], where he serves as county commissioner, with 29% of the vote.{{cite news|date=November 3, 2021|title=Florida Special Primary as a "[[Hail Mary pass]]" and doubted it would be successful. Don James, an attorney for Holness, acknowledged that the challenge likely would not be resolved in time for the election.{{cite web|last=Geggis|first=Anne|title=Dale Holness, Still Appealing Congressional District 20 Loss, Files for 2022 Rematch |url=https://tamaractalk.com/dale-holness-still-appealing-congressional-district-20-loss-files-for-2022-rematch-26685|website=Tamarac Talk|date=December 7, 2021}} [[Mail-in ballot]]s for the special election with Cherfilus-McCormick listed as the Democratic nominee were sent out beginning on December 3.{{cite web| url = https://floridapolitics.com/archives/477965-broward-elections-supervisor-voters-should-decide-elections-not-the-postal-service/| title = Broward elections supervisor: 'Voters should decide elections, not the postal service'| date = December 6, 2021}} On December 6, Cherfilus-McCormick's attorneys filed a lengthy [[legal brief|brief]] in response to the lawsuit that disputed its claims, calling it "a desperate attempt to overturn the will of the voters." In response to the allegation of bribery, the brief points out that promising monetary benefits to voters is common, comparing Cherfilus-McCormick's support for a universal basic income to "a chicken in every pot and a car in every garage," a slogan used by former president [[Herbert Hoover]] in his [[1928 United States presidential election|1928 presidential campaign]]. The brief also claims that Holness's complaint was filed too late and is thus invalid, and asks the judge to dismiss it and order Holness to pay Cherfilus-McCormick's legal fees.{{cite web|last=Man|first=Anthony|date=December 6, 2021|title=Holness plans rematch after losing primary to Cherfilus-McCormick by just 5 votes|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/news/politics/fl-ne-rematch-20th-congressional-district-cherfilus-mccormick-holness-sharief-20211206-l77odfxkb5ggph4sdfawuk754u-story.html|access-date=December 6, 2021|website=[[Sun-Sentinel]]|publisher=Tribune Publishing|language=en-US}} Ultimately, Holness's challenge fell flat, as no judge took up the case.{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/house-election-florida/2022/01/10/22c9ea00-7278-11ec-b202-b9b92330d4fa_story.html |title=Democrat Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick wins House seat in Florida once held by Alcee Hastings |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=2022-01-11 |accessdate=2022-05-27 |author=Weigel, David}} ==Republican primary== ===Campaign=== Two Republicans made the primary ballot, businessman Jason Mariner and Greg Musselwhite, who had been the Republican nominee for the seat in [[2020 United States House of Representatives elections in Florida|2020]]. The two men cut different appearances on the campaign trail, with Mariner presenting himself in a clean-cut fashion while Musselwhite campaigned in a more folksy manner.{{cite web|url=https://floridianpress.com/2021/08/musselwhite-deletes-facebook-attack-against-gop-opponent-mariner/|title=Musselwhite Deletes Facebook Attack Against GOP Opponent Mariner|website=The Floridian|last1=Manjarres|first1=Javier|date=August 26, 2021|accessdate=December 10, 2021}} A substantial part of Mariner's campaign was based around his turning his life around after previously being imprisoned twice on various felony charges.{{cite web|url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/news/2021/11/05/gardens-ex-felon-jason-mariner-florida-gop-dist-20-winner-did-not-follow-state-process/6296359001/|title=Florida GOP Dist 20 winner, Jason Mariner, did not follow process to hold office after jail|website=Palm Beach Post|last1=Bolies|first1=Corbin|date=November 5, 2021|archive-date=November 5, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211105232222/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/news/2021/11/05/gardens-ex-felon-jason-mariner-florida-gop-dist-20-winner-did-not-follow-state-process/6296359001/?utm_campaign=snd-autopilot&utm_source=twitter&utm_medium=Social&utm_campaign=ghf-palmbeach-main|accessdate=December 10, 2021}} Musselwhite attacked Mariner for his prior felony convictions, claiming in a later-deleted [[Facebook]] post that voters had a choice between "the correctional officer or the inmate". Mariner ran as an "America First conservative",{{cite web|url=https://www.tampabay.com/news/florida-politics/2021/11/05/a-florida-felon-won-a-gop-congressional-primary-but-can-he-hold-office/|title=A Florida felon won a GOP congressional primary, but can he hold office?|website=Tampa Bay Times|date=November 5, 2021|accessdate=December 11, 2021}} promoting false claims that the results of the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 presidential election]] were illegitimate, as well as making statements in support of the rioters at the [[2021 United States Capitol attack|2021 U.S. Capitol attack]] and the [[Confederate Flag]], which he defended as a "battle flag that was later co-opted by racist groups".{{cite web|url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/this-confederate-flag-tattood-felon-jason-mariner-is-running-for-congress|title=This Confederate Flag-Tattoo'd Felon Is Running for Congress|website=The Daily Beast|last1=Bolies|first1=Colin|date=November 24, 2021|accessdate=December 12, 2021}} ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== * Jason Mariner, businessman ====Eliminated in primary==== * Gregory "Greg" Musselwhite, [[welding]] inspector and nominee for this district in [[2020 Florida's 20th congressional district election|2020]] ====Disqualified==== * Vic DeGrammont, realtor * Roland Florez{{cite web|title=Candidate Tracking system -
